subject: core-service
note: The realtime engine only. The core-service pack also covers the ConvAI_Middleman API gateway, which is a separate repository with its own routes and models; nothing here extracts from it, so a claim about a REST endpoint on the gateway is still verified by hand. Recording that limit is the point: a contract that silently covers half a subject is worse than none, because the half it misses looks checked.
version_note: No version is extracted. The service's own number lives in pyproject.toml, which is TOML rather than JSON, and it is not a value any page may print anyway: this API is versioned by its routes, not by a package number. Teaching the extractor a TOML parser to read a number nothing is allowed to use would be effort spent making a wrong thing easier.

routes.why: Every route the realtime engine serves, with its method. This is the one set a page can be checked against exactly: a documented endpoint that is not here does not exist.

packages.why: The service's top-level areas. Named explicitly rather than by exclusion so that a new area shows up as a change here rather than being silently swept in.

models.why: Request and response shapes. A field name on an API page comes from one of these, never from memory.

handlers.why: What handles each kind of incoming message. A page describing what happens after a client connects is describing one of these.

services.why: The engine's internal services. Mostly not reader-facing, but a name on a page has to resolve to one of them or it is wrong.

transport.why: Connection and streaming types, which the realtime pages name directly.

must_exist_why: Deliberately empty for now. A must_exist entry is a promise that a rename is an error, and nobody has yet agreed which of this service's internal class names are load-bearing for the documentation. Fill it once the API reference pages are rewritten against this surface - an unearned guard is worse than none, because it looks like coverage.
documented_sets_why: Small and stable. A new top-level area is a real change worth noticing.
coverage_sets_why: Reported as one ratio. Routes are the reader-facing surface of this service, so how much of it the docs mention is the number that matters.
symbol_prefixes_why: Python classes here are mostly unprefixed, so the drift check on prose is deliberately narrow: it catches a wrong Convai-prefixed name and leaves generic ones such as SessionManager to the verifier, where a human decides.
not_covered: ConvAI_Middleman — the REST API gateway. Separate repository, separate routes and models.
Backend behaviour beyond the client contract: which models run, server-side limits, plan gating.
Anything about the dashboard, which belongs to the playground pack.
not_covered_why: Stated so a reader of a clean drift report knows what the report did not look at. A checker that is silent about its own blind spots invites the assumption that it has none.
section_why: Where this subject's pages live in the documentation repository. Declared rather than inferred from the pack name: core-service's pages are under api-reference, and guessing reported its own exemplars as borrowed from another subject.
